citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.2.12 p1  (2.12 THE RERUN CLAUSE)  the text is in p1

citations.quote: the terms 'reel' and 'unit' are synonymous and completely interchangeable
citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.4.2.4 p1  (4.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in p1

cases.reason: Three sentences. (1) SR-14.9.6.3-2 "The words REEL and UNIT are equivalent" states the first, witnessed at 85 by pb141_close_forms. (2) "Treatment of sequential mass storage files is logically equivalent to the treatment of a file on tape" has no 2023 counterpart. (3) The multiple-file-tape sentence describes a form 2023 removed. On this host's disk medium the compiler classes a sequential file as non-reel/unit (status 07 for NO REWIND/REEL/REMOVAL). That matches the 1985 Appendix rationale for status 07 (XVII, item 40, I-O status), which treats such CLOSEs on mass storage as 07 successes. Read against sentence 2 the text is arguable, so the refuter should weigh it.

citations.quote: may be different from the number of character positions in the description of that record
citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.1.3.1 p3  (1.3.1 Organization)  the text is in p3

cases.reason: "the number of character positions reserved on the medium to store a particular logical record may be different from the number of character positions in the description". This is a permission to the implementor: no output can violate it. It is not a definition of a property of the user's program, it has no unpopulatable antecedent, it names no other row, and it does not say 'undefined', so no derivation arm fits. GR-13.18.43.4-2 grants a similar latitude in 2023, but for a different reason (control information) and witnessed only on sequential files. What would settle it: a ruling that an implementor permission closes by derivation (or by a read-back witness such as relcon.cob).

cases.needs: a ruling: derivation arm for an implementor-latitude permission, or acceptance of a read-back witness
